author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected. Its date and description can be changed under the same rules as booking, the correction replaces what the visit held rather than adding a second visit, and an accepted correction returns to the owner's record. The correction form is reached by direct address; nothing links to it.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit holds the submitted values and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when an accepted correction is submitted, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the date is named
given a refused correction, when the refusal is shown, then the correction form is shown again rather than the owner's record
given an owner whose pet has a visit, when the owner's record is opened, then it carries no link to the correction form
edge case 3: a visit whose date has already passed can only be corrected by giving it a date later than today
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope (NG-5)
the owner detail page gains no link to the correction form in this round; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request
no change to what a visit holds beyond its date and description
notes: NG-5 narrowing recorded the project's way: a new non-goal ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-16-non-goal-visit-correction.md), the rewritten NG-5 row, and the Non-Goals preamble. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope and still needs adding. Three questions the owner left open are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than consulted: whether a visible entry point follows, whether a correction is refused when the visit does not belong to the named pet or owner, and whether an already-passed visit should be correctable at all. Behavior not stated by the owner was not invented.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correcting a Visit reuses the in-place child-edit shape PetController already runs. An id-branching @ModelAttribute loader resolves the child from the Owner aggregate, request binding lands on that loaded instance, and OwnerRepository.save cascades the update. No new module, pattern, layer, or dependency. The adjustment is one parameter and one accessor: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId path variable, and Pet gains getVisit(Integer) mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for VisitController, Visit, Pet, and OwnerRepository now carry REQ-VISITEDIT-001, and the by-identity child-navigation invariant is recorded alongside them. The product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-16-non-goal-visit-correction.md, which now has its index row in docs/adr/README.md. No new ADR: the how is consistency with an existing in-force pattern, with no trade-off to record.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit are added to VisitController; both create routes stay unchanged
loadPetWithVisit takes visitId as a not-required Integer path variable. Null keeps today's behaviour (fresh Visit attached to the pet). Present returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and attaches nothing
the edit POST keeps a Visit-typed parameter so Spring resolves the model attribute named visit and binds onto the loaded instance rather than instantiating a fresh one
owners.save(owner) merges the detached aggregate; the corrected Visit keeps its identity, so the cascade issues an UPDATE against the existing row
the form template posts to the current URL and carries no action attribute, so createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is expected to need no change at all
ownerDetails.html stays untouched; leaving it alone is what satisfies the no-link criterion
minVisitDate already applies to every handler in the controller, so the edit form gets the same date floor as the booking form

patterns.description: findPet — the id-branching @ModelAttribute loader to copy: new instance when the path variable is absent, the aggregate child when present
initUpdateForm and processUpdateForm — the create/edit route pair on one controller sharing one form template and one redirect target
getPet(Integer) — the by-identity child lookup that Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors, returning null when absent
the non-future date rejection. Extract it into one private method both handlers call; do not duplicate the block
shouldAddNewVisitForPet — the @DataJpaTest visit-count assertion shape, available if the persistence-level no-extra-row guarantee is wanted beyond the web slice

risks.risk: The controller InitBinder disallows id and *.id, so a Visit that Spring instantiates for the edit POST always arrives with no identity. Attaching such an instance to the pet inserts a second visit row — the exact failure the slice forbids.
risks.mitigation: Bind onto the Visit that loadPetWithVisit returned. Call neither pet.addVisit nor owner.addVisit on the correction path, and keep the handler parameter Visit-typed so the model attribute is reused.

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit today attaches a fresh blank Visit to the pet unconditionally. Reused as-is, the edit GET pollutes the aggregate and the edit POST cascades a blank row that fails the description constraint.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId before constructing anything; only the create branch constructs and attaches.

risks.risk: A visitId belonging to a different pet or owner would let one aggregate be corrected through another aggregate's URL.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only within pet.getVisits(), so the owner-pet-visit path must hold. Throw IllegalArgumentException when it does not, matching the pet-not-found handling already in the same method. This is the narrowest reading of the PRD open question on mismatched ownership, not a new product decision.

risks.risk: Setting a Validator on the visit data binder, mirroring PetValidator, would displace bean validation and silently drop the @NotBlank description rule.
risks.mitigation: Keep @Valid and the entity constraints. Add no VisitValidator in this slice.

risks.risk: A new message key for an edit-specific button label or heading would breach REQ-LANG-002 unless added to all eleven bundles, and the bundle-parity test would fail the build.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the template and its existing keys. No acceptance criterion asks for different wording on the correction form.

risks.risk: The web-slice test mocks OwnerRepository, so it cannot observe a duplicate INSERT at the JPA level.
risks.mitigation: The visit-count assertion runs against the real in-memory Owner the mock returns and catches the modelling error directly. A @DataJpaTest case alongside shouldAddNewVisitForPet covers the persistence level if the stronger guarantee is wanted.

risks.risk: On the refusal path the binder has already mutated the loaded Visit in place, so the redisplayed form shows the rejected values.
risks.mitigation: That is the intended redisplay. No save runs on the error path and open-in-view is disabled, so the detached mutation never reaches the database.

notes: Verdict is minor rather than covered because two source-level adjustments are required, not because new ground is broken. Pattern check: no new type is introduced, so the catalog's In force list is untouched. Controller-rule check: architecture-principles.md records that a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the existing deviation. The correction adds no new rule — it reuses the REQ-VIS-001 date check — which is why the guidance is to extract the existing check rather than write a second one. Security check against security-principles.md Realization: Widening the exposed surface — two routes under the existing owner/pet path, mutating a visit under the same open-route demonstration baseline as visit booking, no broader exposure. Trusting cross-request state — owner, pet, and visit are re-resolved from the repository on every request, with no reliance on a prior request. Mass assignment — the controller's unnamed @InitBinder already covers every handler, so the new routes inherit the id disallow list without a per-endpoint addition. No row leaves the application weaker than the baseline. Flash message: both sibling routes set a hard-coded confirmation on redirect, and no criterion covers one here. If the implementer adds one, it follows the sibling shape rather than introducing a message key mid-slice. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Vocabulary: ubiquitous-language.md lists Booking on the Avoid line for Visit, so code and prose say Visit and correction.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: loadPetWithVisit's id-branching mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer)/PetController.findPet exactly, with the visit-scoping invariant (resolved only within pet.getVisits()) documented in the method javadoc

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Defense in depth, unchanged-from-baseline: processUpdateVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and then owners.save(owner), so request parameters bind onto the loaded Owner and a caller can rewrite owner fields (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone) through the visit URL. This is identical to the existing processNewVisitForm and is consistent with the project's pattern, so it is not a regression against the recorded baseline in docs/system-design.md Security Context. If a future slice tightens it, tighten both handlers together (an allow-list binder for the Owner attribute, or re-reading the owner instead of binding it).

Supply chain: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match was run this pass. The slice adds no dependency, so the check is not triggered by this change; closing it against the NVD (Spring Boot 4.1.0, Jackson) remains a CI or human task.
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization holds on the new routes: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner -> pet -> visit strictly within the aggregate (owners.findById, owner.getPet, pet.getVisit), so a visitId belonging to another pet or owner is unreachable through /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. VisitControllerTests.theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotOnTheNamedPet exercises the mismatch.

Mass assignment on the identifier stays closed: the controller's existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") covers both new handlers, so the corrected Visit keeps the identity the loader resolved and binding cannot retarget another row.
Trusting cross-request state is avoided: the edit POST re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the repository on every request rather than trusting the identifiers a prior GET validated.
No new injection surface: no string-concatenated query text, no shell or ProcessBuilder use, no file or path handling, no deserialization entry point, no logging of request-derived values.
Output escaping unchanged: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is untouched and uses th:text throughout; no th:utext, no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__), no request-derived value in an href.

Validation parity between booking and correction: rejectDateThatIsNotInTheFuture is a single extracted method both handlers call, so the date floor cannot drift between the two paths, and @Valid still applies the entity constraints on the correction.

New IllegalArgumentException message carries only int/Integer path variables ('Visit with id N not found for pet with id M.'), so the error page that renders exception messages gains no sensitive value and no attacker-controlled text.
No new mutable controller state; the singleton VisitController stays thread-confined.
No dependency, build, or configuration change: build.gradle is not in the change set, so the resolved dependency set is unchanged by this slice.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 ('a visit whose date has already passed can only be corrected by giving it a date later than today') has no dedicated test case. Every fixture visit uses BOOKED_VISIT_DATE = LocalDate.now().plusDays(7); no test ever books a visit whose date is already in the past and then corrects it. The existing 'date not in the future' refusal test only proves today's-date is rejected on a future-dated original visit, which is a different scenario from the PRD's edge case.
findings.fix: Add a test (e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldSucceedWhenCorrectingAPastDatedVisitToAFutureDate) that seeds a visit with a past date, corrects it to a future date, and asserts success — proving a lapsed visit is reachable and correctable, not just that non-future dates are rejected on already-future visits.

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer), the new id-matching lookup the whole correction feature depends on, is only ever exercised against a pet holding a single visit. No test seeds a pet with two or more visits and asserts getVisit(id) returns the correct one — the disambiguation branch (Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)) and the isNew() guard are unexercised. A defect that returned the wrong visit, or matched the first visit regardless of id, would pass every current test.
findings.fix: Add a case (unit test on Pet, or a VisitControllerTests case) where the pet holds two visits with distinct ids and assert the correction form/POST operates on the one named by visitId, leaving the other visit's date and description untouched.

findings.description: testing-principles.md (Test Data Construction / Factory Methods) requires new or modified test construction to go behind a factory method, applying to tests modified from 2026-07-31 onward. init() was touched in this slice to add bookedVisit construction (new Visit(); setId/setDate/setDescription; pet.addVisit(...)) via direct constructor calls rather than a factory. The equivalent new construction in OwnerControllerTests.java's georgesVisit fixture (visit.setId(TEST_VISIT_ID)) touches the same pattern.
findings.fix: Wrap the booked-visit construction in a factory method (e.g. createABookedVisit(date, description)) that the test suite owns, matching the brief's Factory Methods rule for newly added/modified construction.

approved_aspects: All six PRD-listed test names are present and each maps to a distinct acceptance criterion
theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotOnTheNamedPet directly tests the cross-aggregate risk flagged in the design triage (visit resolved only within pet.getVisits())
Visit-count-unchanged and date/description-replaced assertions read the real Owner/Pet/Visit graph the mocked repository returns rather than verifying a mock interaction, honoring tested-as-spec
AssertJ used throughout for state assertions, with singleElement().satisfies(...) keeping the correction assertions on one object
No mystery literals: all dates and descriptions are named constants derived relative to LocalDate.now()
./gradlew test passes for both touched test classes

findings.description: The Open Question 'Is a correction refused when the visit does not belong to the named pet or owner?' states 'nothing yet says whether correction does.' This is contradicted by the shipped, tested behavior in this same change set: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit throws IllegalArgumentException for a visitId not found on the named pet, and VisitControllerTests.theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotOnTheNamedPet asserts exactly that refusal. author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain, unchanged from round 1: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran this pass. The fix delta adds no dependency and touches no build file, so nothing new is triggered; closing Spring Boot 4.1.0 and Jackson against the NVD remains a CI or human task.

approved_aspects: Fix delta carries no production code: the only changed files are docs/prd.md and three test sources (OwnerControllerTests, the new PetTests, VisitControllerTests). VisitController.java and Pet.java are byte-identical to the tree approved in round 1, so the object-level authorization path (owners.findById -> owner.getPet -> pet.getVisit) and the @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") mass-assignment guard are unchanged and still hold.

No new attack surface in the delta: no route, binder, query, file, path, process, deserialization, or logging change. Detection-pattern sweep over the delta found no shell execution, no string-built query text, no file or /tmp handling, no polymorphic Jackson configuration.

No secrets in the delta: the added constants are visit ids, future/past LocalDate offsets, and descriptive strings ("Annual checkup", "Dental cleaning", "Rescheduled checkup", "Checkup the owner missed"). No token, password, key, credential, connection string, or hostname is introduced.

Test helpers are safe: createABookedVisit / bookAVisitForTestPet / visitOfTestPet build and read in-memory domain objects only, hold no shared mutable static state (constants are immutable Integer/String/LocalDate), and use a stream filter with orElseThrow rather than an unguarded get.

The new PetTests pins the null-visitId contract (aPetShouldNeverOfferAVisitThatWasNeverBooked asserts pet.getVisit(null) is null), which is the fail-secure behaviour the create route depends on: a missing visitId resolves to no stored visit rather than to an arbitrary one. This strengthens the round-1 evidence rather than weakening it.

VisitControllerTests adds two correction cases (a lapsed visit corrected into the future, and a correction that must leave the pet's other visits untouched) that exercise by-identity child navigation over a multi-visit pet. The second is a direct regression test for the wrong-object-updated class, which is the abuse shape behind the object-level authorization claim.

The docs/prd.md change is text only: it promotes the visit/pet/owner mismatch refusal from an Open Question to Visits edge case 4, matching the shipped and tested behaviour, and adjusts the open-question count wording. No new commitment weakens a security property recorded in docs/security-principles.md or the docs/system-design.md Security Context.
